summary:
Earth Jukebox is a web app that loads NASA GIBS satellite frames live and analyses their pixels for colour, brightness, ice and cloud cover, heat and edges.
It converts those measurements into sound in the browser with the Web Audio API: colour sets the note on a minor scale, brightness opens the tone, ice deepens a drone, heat adds tension, and edges quicken the pulse.
A scan line sweeps the frame left to right in 64 slices over 8 seconds, and the sound follows what it crosses.
Four presets (Arctic sea ice, global temperature, wildfires, ocean colour) and a time slider covering 2000–2026 let users step through months by keyboard or mouse.
The app shows a text description of each frame, an audio legend, speech announcements, contrast and reduced-motion options, and haptics on supported phones.
It exports the sound as a WAV file, and the readout as Braille text, an SVG, and 3D-printable STL and OBJ files, using NASA GIBS, EONET and POWER data plus Open-Meteo weather.
